context: After the damaged landing you repaired a radio, built its charger, and established a signal on the crash ridge. The inner cabin survived.

events.message: Radio. Replace the damaged detachable lead; the radio itself is repaired, not duplicated.
Solar charger. Connect the salvaged collector to its compatible storage unit.
Solar radio. Fit an internal power supply to the radio.
Placed. We hear you. That light above the ridge means someone is still there—and now we can answer.
We take the useful equipment onward to somewhere to come back to, leaving the earlier work where it stands. We collect the things needed for this scene along the way.
Placed.
Meltwater. Connect our recovered solar charger to the small fixed enclosed melt head. Over the narrated collection interval it provides the batch for the habitat canister.
Filtered water. The mission filter processes this known source inside its enclosed vessel; not real water-safety advice.
Water canister. Seal the water against dust and evaporation.
Seed tray. The tray contains prepared terrestrial growing medium.
Watered seed tray. Water the prepared tray.
No new combination here.
Placed.
Sprouted tray. Time passes in the warm pressurized cabin; no instant real germination is implied.
Propagator. Protect the living tray from the disturbed entrance air.
No new combination here.
Pressure patch. Prepare a compatible patch for the damaged outer vestibule.
Sealed panel. Work the compatible seam closed.
Vestibule. Fit the repaired outer entrance around the existing hatch.
No new combination here.
Anchored vestibule. Anchor the fabric structure to its prepared footings.

Insulated vestibule. Wrap the outer structure; the inner cabin still supplies pressure and life support. The entry is weather-tight, the water is stored, and the little tray has a sheltered home. Our signal now marks a refuge, not a crash site.
